top_module.name: adaptive_aero_control_top
top_module.description: Top-level integration of CPU subsystem, CSR/MMIO control plane, request/response supervision, actuator clamping, safety aggregation, and technology-neutral buffering.
top_module.functionality: Implements the system-level adaptive aero control contract: firmware-mediated CSR/MMIO control, validated request/response transport, explicit timeout and freshness rejection, clamped actuator command generation, deterministic safe fallback, and fault/health reporting. The top remains in safe fallback on reset, CPU unavailability, invalid responses, stale data, or timeout conditions.
responsibilities: Expose a real Wishbone CSR/MMIO interface to firmware.
Integrate the PicoRV32 subsystem boundary and its observable status.
Validate external model responses before any actuator update.
Clamp and optionally rate-limit validated actuator commands.
Maintain deterministic safe fallback on reset and on fault conditions.
Generate interrupt output from safety/fault status.
must_not_drive: Do not bypass firmware-mediated acceptance with a direct hardware control path.
Do not expose geometry arrays, tensors, or unbounded payloads at top level.
Do not emit active actuator commands while reset, faulted, or uninitialized.
Do not claim board readiness without the full CPU/memory/control-plane synthesis integration.
top_module.reset_behavior: All state resets to safe fallback. No request is issued, no actuator update is valid, watchdog supervision is inactive, and fault outputs reset to the safe state until firmware initializes and enables operation.
behavior_rules: Wishbone accesses are deterministically acknowledged by the CSR/MMIO block.
Response acceptance requires validity, matching sequence policy, freshness, operating-point envelope compliance, and clean integrity bits.
Timeout and stale-data faults latch until firmware clears them after the underlying condition has cleared.
Validated actuator commands are clamped to CSR-programmed bounds before output.
If CPU is halted or uninitialized, the design remains in safe fallback.
No floating-point datapath is permitted.

modules.name: aero_cpu_subsystem
modules.description: PicoRV32 Wishbone CPU subsystem boundary for firmware execution, CSR/MMIO access, optional UART diagnostics, and interrupt reception.
modules.functionality: Represents the integrated PicoRV32 rv32imc soft CPU subsystem boundary. Firmware uses the Wishbone master interface to configure the control plane, issue requests, clear faults, and monitor status. The module reports halt and initialization status for safety supervision.
responsibilities: Generate Wishbone master transactions for firmware access.
Provide CPU halt and initialization status.
Receive interrupt sources for response-ready, fault, and timeout events.
Provide optional UART diagnostics.
Remain inactive from an actuator-control standpoint.
must_not_drive: Do not directly command actuators.
Do not bypass the CSR/MMIO contract.
Do not expose geometry or payload tensors.
modules.reset_behavior: CPU outputs idle on reset; halted and uninitialized status assert until firmware and subsystem initialization complete.
behavior_rules: Wishbone master behavior must conform to rv32imc firmware execution requirements.
Interrupt input aggregation is level-safe and deterministic.
CPU status must be observable by top-level safety logic.

modules.name: control_plane_csr
modules.description: Wishbone CSR/MMIO register block that decodes firmware-visible control and status registers for adaptive aero control and emits explicit semantic control outputs.
modules.functionality: Decodes the firmware-visible register bank and publishes semantic control signals used by the request issuer, watchdog, actuator clamp logic, and status reporting. Read data returns configuration and status fields. Writes configure enable, timeout, freshness, sequence, geometry reference, operating-point envelope, actuator bounds, rate limiting, fallback command, overwrite policy, and fault clearing.
responsibilities: Provide a real MMIO/CSR decode window reachable by firmware through Wishbone.
Expose all implemented registers and fields in the authoritative register contract.
Translate raw register writes into explicit semantic outputs.
Return status registers for response sequence, age, fault summary, and health summary.
Clear faults only when firmware requests it and the fault source has cleared.
must_not_drive: Do not directly drive actuator outputs.
Do not directly drive request/response stream pins.
Do not hide inaccessible internal state as software-visible registers.
modules.reset_behavior: All registers reset to safe defaults: enable off, watchdog conservative, freshness conservative, overwrite policy stalled, request sequence cleared, fallback command configured, and fault clear deasserted.
behavior_rules: Every declared register must be reachable through RTL decode.
The register map must be compact and implementation-friendly.
Read-only status fields must reflect live safety state.
Fault-clear writes are accepted only when the fault source has cleared.

modules.name: request_response_supervisor
modules.description: Bounded valid/ready stream policy engine that issues request packets, tracks outstanding sequence state, enforces freshness and watchdog timeout, and validates response packets before they are eligible for actuator use.
modules.functionality: Constructs the bounded external request packet, accepts an incoming bounded response packet, and performs sequencing, age, operating-point envelope, and integrity checks. It maintains outstanding request state, watchdog timeout counting, and explicit reject/accept indicators. The response is only marked validated when all policy checks pass; otherwise a specific fault bit is asserted and the response is rejected.
responsibilities: Issue a single bounded request stream per accepted firmware command.
Track outstanding request sequence and age.
Support stall or overwrite policy for a new request while one is outstanding.
Set explicit reject and fault outputs for invalid, stale, or mismatched responses.
Start and monitor watchdog timing on each request issuance.
Provide validated actuator surface outputs to the clamping stage.
must_not_drive: Do not generate actuator outputs directly.
Do not accept responses without validating status, sequence, age, operating-point envelope, and integrity bits.
Do not expose geometry arrays or tensors.
Do not exceed 128-bit packet width.
modules.reset_behavior: On reset, no request is issued, no response is accepted, outstanding sequence and counters clear, timeout is inactive, and all fault outputs reset to safe inactive state.
behavior_rules: A response is accepted only when validity is asserted, sequence policy matches, age is within threshold, operating point is inside the configured envelope, and integrity bits are clear.
Rejected responses must explicitly assert the corresponding fault bit(s) and response_rejected.
Timeout must start on each request issuance and assert timeout_fault if the matching response does not arrive in time.
If overwrite policy is disabled, new request issuance while outstanding shall stall; if enabled, it may overwrite with explicit request_overwritten indication.
Request and response packet formats must be fixed-slice, integer-only, and documented in the register contract.

modules.name: actuator_command_clamper
modules.description: Applies programmable min/max bounds and optional rate-of-change limiting to validated actuator commands and selects the safe fallback command whenever the system is not in a valid drive condition.
modules.functionality: Implements integer-only clamping and optional rate limiting for each actuator channel. When no validated update is present, or when any fault is active, it drives the deterministic fallback command and asserts safe_fallback.
responsibilities: Clamp each actuator command to configured bounds.
Apply optional rate limiting before output.
Hold or drive the fallback command when validation is absent or faulted.
Assert explicit clamp and rate-limit fault indicators when commands exceed permitted bounds or step size.
must_not_drive: Do not source outputs from unvalidated stream contents.
Do not violate configured bounds or rate limits.
Do not bypass safe fallback on reset or fault.
modules.reset_behavior: Reset forces the fallback command to the outputs, deasserts valid, and asserts safe_fallback.
behavior_rules: Output updates occur only when validated_update and response_validated are both asserted and fault_active is low.
Each channel must be clamped independently to its min/max range.
If rate limiting is enabled, output delta per update must not exceed cfg_rate_limit_step.
When any fault is active, the fallback command is driven regardless of input command values.

modules.name: safety_fault_manager
modules.description: Aggregates validation, timeout, stale-data, clamp, and CPU/runtime status into a latched fault summary and health summary, and generates interrupt causes.
modules.functionality: Latches and reports fault causes, computes health summary, and generates interrupt request lines for response-ready, fault, and timeout events. It enforces the policy that faults may only be cleared when firmware requests clear and the underlying condition is no longer present.
responsibilities: Aggregate and latch fault conditions deterministically.
Generate dedicated interrupt causes for response-ready, fault, and timeout events.
Expose read-only fault and health summaries to firmware.
Permit fault clearing only after the fault source has disappeared and firmware has issued a clear request.
must_not_drive: Do not directly modify actuator outputs.
Do not clear faults unconditionally.
Do not use floating point or non-deterministic behavior.
modules.reset_behavior: All fault latches clear to the safe state on reset, interrupts deassert, and fault_active is low.
behavior_rules: CPU halted or not initialized shall force the safe fallback path.
Faults latch until firmware clear is requested and the condition has cleared.
Interrupt outputs must be deterministic and directly attributable to specific conditions.

modules.name: transport_buffer_wrapper
modules.description: Technology-neutral bounded memory/buffer wrapper for minimal request, response, and history storage intended for FPGA BRAM mapping.
modules.functionality: Provides bounded FIFO/history buffering semantics that map to native FPGA block RAM. This wrapper never exposes unbounded arrays or geometry tensors, and it only handles compact transport/history records needed for supervision and bring-up.
responsibilities: Map bounded payload buffering to technology-neutral BRAM-style interfaces.
Avoid register-array flattening for bulk payload/history storage.
Provide full/empty and validity indicators for controller use.
Keep buffering minimal and bounded for FPGA prototype implementation.
must_not_drive: Do not replace memory macros with plain register arrays in the contract.
Do not widen the transport beyond the declared bounded widths.
Do not expose geometry arrays or tensors.
modules.reset_behavior: Buffer pointers, valid flags, and history state reset to empty and invalid. All buffer and memory control outputs are idle until commanded by the controller.
behavior_rules: Storage is bounded and minimal.
The wrapper is technology-neutral and intended for FPGA BRAM inference/mapping.
History and payload buffering exist only to support the controller contract and must not become a data-plane bypass.
